title: The Galois group of x(x-1)...(x-p+1)+1
description:
Let p be an odd prime and fp(x) = x(x−1)···(x−p+1) + 1. This record contains a research note on Gal(fp/Q), together with the data and standalone verification tools for every computational claim in it.

Main results.

  • A general certificate: a monic irreducible of odd prime degree p whose Frobenius at an odd unramified prime q is both odd (Stickelberger) and fixed-point-free has Galois group Sp. The group-theoretic input is that every transitive nonsolvable subgroup of Sp is Sp or lies in Ap, with the classification of finite simple groups entering only through Guralnick's theorem on subgroups of prime power index.
  • For fp the fixed-point-free condition is automatic at every q ≤ p, because the p consecutive factors cover every residue class. The whole question therefore reduces to a single Kronecker symbol (disc fp / q) = −1 with q < p.
  • That symbol is periodic in p for fixed q. For q = 3 the period is 36 and the good classes are p ≡ 7, 13, 17, 19, 23, 29 (mod 36), giving a computer-free proof that Gal(fp/Q) = Sp on a set of primes of Dirichlet density 1/2. Adding q = 5 (period 600) raises the density to 31/40.
  • Gal(fp/Q) = Sp is verified for every odd prime p < 100000, each by a witness q ≤ 47 recorded in the accompanying witness list.
  • Several standard approaches are shown to be closed for this family: fp is totally real for p ≥ 5, so complex conjugation is not a transposition; the Newton polygons of every relevant translate are flat; and while the family φ(x) − t is Morse with Galois group Sp over Q(t), Hilbert irreducibility does not decide the single specialisation t = −1.
  • What remains open for all p is a covering question: do the periodic good classes, as q varies, cover every prime?

Every certificate is verifiable row by row, independently of the searches that produced the data: each witness row is one resultant and one Legendre symbol over a small finite field. The included tools re-check all of it, including a full audit of the 9,590-row witness list.
notes: Companion data and verification tools are included in the ancillary/ and tools/ directories. Related MathOverflow question: https://mathoverflow.net/questions/514611
